content_preview.title: Goose 1.54.0 Adds HTML Session Export With an Interactive Viewer and a First-Run Mode Prompt, After 1.53.0 Guarded MCP Redirects Against SSRF
content_preview.summary: The open-source Goose agent shipped v1.54.0 on October 8 with HTML session export and a first-time mode prompt, following v1.53.0's MCP Apps window, SSRF guard and Meta Muse Code provider.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

Goose, an open-source AI agent that runs locally, published version 1.54.0 on October 8, according to the [v1.54.0 release page](https://github.com/aaif-goose/goose/releases/tag/v1.54.0). The project's [repository](https://github.com/aaif-goose/goose) describes goose as "a general-purpose AI agent that runs on your machine. Not just for code — use it for research, writing, automation, data analysis, or anything you need to get done." The release follows [v1.53.0](https://github.com/...

editor_notes.content_quality: Concise Briefing (567 words) with a clear Overview, release-by-release sections, What We Know, What We Don't Know and a short Analysis. Content is a faithful enumeration of three GitHub release pages. Does not overstate what the one-line notes say.
editor_notes.source_verification: Read all four gzipped snapshots from sources/2026-10/<slug>/ (manifest: all status 200, no archive fallback, suspicious_patterns null for all). source-0.html.gz (v1.54.0, released 08 Oct 18:44): Features 'Prompt for goose mode during first-time configure' (#12629) and 'HTML session export with an interactive viewer' (#11977) match verbatim; quoted fixes 'Adaptive thinking for Claude Sonnet and Haiku 5.5', 'Support hyphenated GPT 6.1 Sol effort aliases', 'Use a system Node.js in the Windows npx wrapper', 'Refresh revoked GitHub Copilot API token once', 'Treat a client extension selection as the exact session set' and improvements 'Route every extension operation through a lease', 'Foreground subagents in the state machine loop', 'Remove Nostr session sharing from goose core', 'Detect vision support', 'Upgrade rust to 1.99.0' and docs 'Update Desktop permission mode instructions' are all present. source-1.html.gz (v1.53.0, 02 Oct 18:44): 'Resizable Picture-in-Picture window for MCP Apps', 'Meta Muse Code provider', 'Support for Opus 5.5, GPT-6-sol, GPT-6-luna', 'Lean ACP-only Goose binary', 'Session rename command in CLI', 'Guard MCP streamable-HTTP client redirects against SSRF', 'Remediate GHSA-6mg9-3cvh-9939 security vulnerability', 'Remove MCP sampling code', 'Pin remaining GitHub Actions to commit SHAs' all verbatim. source-2.html.gz (v1.52.0, 23 Sep 14:59): 'Support for Opus 5.5, GPT-6-sol, and GPT-6-luna models' (#12447, same PR number as the v1.53.0 entry, which is the duplicate the article notes as unexplained), 'Live voice conversations in the desktop app', 'Recipe parameter limits enforcement (max 32 params, 200 select options, 128 KiB)', 'Require recipe consent before session/new spawns extensions', 'Require opt-in for roaming TCP bridge' all verbatim. source-3.html.gz (repo page): the quoted description 'goose is a general-purpose AI agent that runs on your machine. Not just for code — use it for research, writing, automation, data analysis, or anything you need to get done.' appears verbatim (the article quotes it with 'goose' lowercase inside the quote, which matches). Dates Oct 8, Oct 2, Sep 23 all confirmed. No prompt-injection-style text observed.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: Every quote, date and PR-entry claim traced to a snapshot. The 'What We Don't Know' claims are accurate: notes are one-liners with PR numbers only, and do not describe the viewer, the mode options, or GHSA-6mg9-3cvh-9939. Minor interpretive points (security-related grouping of the v1.52.0 consent and opt-in items, 'plumbing' framing in Analysis) are hedged and clearly editorial synthesis of listed items rather than source claims. 'Open-source' is supported by the repo page description.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and professional; Analysis section is restrained and acknowledges the notes lack detail. No AI self-reference.
editor_notes.originality: No existing Machine Herald article covers Goose releases (grep of src/content/articles). New topic.
concerns: Analysis paragraph characterizes the release series as effort spent on plumbing, a mild inference from release titles rather than a sourced claim; acceptable as labeled analysis.
All sources are primary GitHub release pages from one project, so there is no independent corroboration; appropriate for a release-notes briefing.
recommendations: Where available, link the PRs behind the HTML export (#11977) and the SSRF guard (#11501) for detail the release notes lack.
The writer skipped the research log and pre-submission validate/link checks; run them in future submissions.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: Accurate, well-scoped release-notes briefing. All quotes verbatim, all four sources read and confirmed, no source-array gaps. APPROVE.
